newsitem.title: USA: GE Capital acquires Colonial Penn for $950 million.
newsitem.headline: GE Capital acquires Colonial Penn for $950 million.

text.p: GE Capital said Monday it agreed to acquire Colonial Penn P&C Group from Leucadia National Corp. for $950 million in cash, putting it on the road to directly market personal auto insurance.

GE Capital, known for its large reinsurance and life insurance holdings, said Norristown, Pa.-based Colonial Penn will become a subsidiary of its Richmond, Va.-based Consumer Savings and Insurance Group.
However, GE Capital said it will keep the management and operational platform of Colonial Penn, a fast-growing, low-cost direct marketer of auto insurance like Geico.
Leucadia National said it expects to report a pretax gain of about $600 million upon completion of the sale of Colonial Penn P&C.
The transaction, which is subject to Leucadia shareholder approval and regulatory approvals, is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
Leucadia said it may record the gain in either the third or fourth quarters.

The terms of the transaction call for 1997 earnings to remain in Colonial Penn P&C Group, with GE Capital paying interest on the purchase price at a rate of 6 percent a year from Jan. 1, 1997 to closing.
GE Capital, a subsidiary of General Electric Co.( ), said it expects Colonial Penn to make an immediate contribution to its earnings following completion of the deal.
Prudential Securities analyst Nicholas Heymann said he believes Colonial Penn will contribute about 1 cent a share to GE's earnings in 1998. In 1996, GE earned $2.20 a share, or $7.28 billion.
In addition, Heymann said he believes GE Capital can achieve cost savings of about $30 million as it takes over Colonial Penn's investment management and consolidates some back office operations.
Colonial Penn has premiums of $515 million and pretax earnings of about $73 million.
GE Capital's acquisition of Colonial Penn comes just one week after General Motors Corp.'s General Motors Acceptance Corp. subsidiary agreed to buy non-standard auto insurer Integon Corp..

But the entrance of an aggressive financial services giant like GE Capital is likely to turn up the competitive pressure on other auto insurers like Allstate Corp. and Progressive Corp. ( ), Lehman analyst Peter Wade said.
"I think some of the bigger and better auto insurers have got to be sitting there a little scared right now," Wade said.
But, he said, Colonial Penn offers GE Capital the opportunity for high returns and fast growth.
"I think this is an excellent investment," he said. "I think they saw it as one they couldn't let go.
"This is probably the best sector of the insurance business in terms of long-term potential," he said.
